findings.title: Translation cache key ignores the fallback chain (site default locale)
findings.body:
With fallbacks enabled, the result of `I18n.t(key)` now depends on `SiteSetting.default_locale`, not only on `config.locale`. The LRU cache key is still only `key + locale + backend.object_id`.

After an admin changes the default locale, keys that fell back are still served from the old fallback locale until the cache evicts them.

In a multisite deployment the cache is process-wide, so one site's fallback translations are returned to other sites that have a different default locale.

Fix: include the fallback chain (or the site default locale) in the cache key.

findings.title: Fallback locales are only loaded in the controller filter; jobs/mailers miss them and cache the miss
findings.body:
`I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is called only from `ApplicationController#set_locale`. `I18n.translate` itself only loads `config.locale`.

Code that translates outside a controller request, such as Sidekiq jobs, mailers and rake tasks, gets a fallback chain that points at locales that may never have been loaded. Fallback then quietly fails and returns 'translation missing'.

Worse, the no-args path caches that result in the LRU cache and freezes it. The missing string keeps being served even after the fallback locale is loaded later in the same process.

Fix: load the fallback locales inside `translate` (or `load_locale`) rather than relying on a controller filter.
